hints.title: Cubic Search and Duplication Obstacle
hints.text: Testing every combination of three numbers takes cubic time and produces duplicate triplets. How can sorting first simplify both avoiding duplicates and searching for the remaining sum?

hints.title: Fix One Element and Inward Two Pointers
hints.text: Sort the array and fix the first element. The remaining subproblem reduces to finding pairs that sum to the negated fixed value across the remaining sorted suffix.

hints.title: Sorted Traversal with Adjacent Duplicate Skipping
hints.text: Sort the array. Loop through index i from 0 to n - 3, skipping duplicate values for nums[i]. For each i, search the range from i + 1 to n - 1 with inward pointers. When a valid triplet is found, record it and skip duplicate adjacent elements before continuing.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of nums array (3 <= N <= 3000)
complexity.notes: Sorting takes O(N log N). Outer loop runs N times with an inner O(N) two-pointer scan, giving O(N^2) total time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Checking all triplets with three nested loops takes O(N^3) time. For N = 3000, N^3 = 2.7 * 10^10 operations, which times out immediately. Handling duplicates with set insertions adds massive memory overhead.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Sorting in O(N log N) time enables duplicate skipping in O(1) space during the O(N^2) two-pointer pass, avoiding large hash set storage for triplet deduplication.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Deduplicating in place without auxiliary sets, sorting before traversal, early break when nums[i] > 0, and handling pointer adjustments after matching triplets.

solutions.approach: Sorted Outer Loop + Inward Two Pointers
